# Complete native Level constructor and production composition

`LevelConstructorV3` executes the whole captured Level C1 `3f3128`, against
the SAME `CanonicalLevelContextV1` field authority. Its callbacks require the
actual embedded LuaScript, Application LevelList/online/player/matching owners,
and the actual Save allocation/C1. This is source initialization, not Level Init,
active world publication or gameplay readiness.

`CanonicalLevelContextV1::create` still makes the historical retained prefix.
Call `construct_source_v3(arguments, services, error)` exactly once, before the
subsequent original initialization stages. Its constructor borrow aliases the
same config38/music11c/safe120/ambient124/gate150/module offset/id cells already
used by the loader. Do not instantiate a second Level or replay a failed C1.
External borrows pin the containing Level. The once-only constructor drops its
temporary service captures at return; no self-owning Level lease is retained.

Source ordering includes EventManager C2 on the Level base, LuaScript C1(false),
the direct fields, increment of the actual static debug-load counter, assignment
of `data/scripts/` through the SAME script, and the two original combat/death
loads. Level+ac belongs to LuaScript44's path: there is no second Level path
string. It resets the SAME Module::s_moduleId at its reached store, matches the
first lowercased LevelList filename substring, then follows the actual online
hosting/matching branches. The selected difficulty/row and request flags are
retained. Save allocation occurs before rereading seed/difficulty/row/mode;
successful Save C1 publishes that SAME allocation into field_ec afterwards.

`LevelConstructorBindingsV4` composes the genuine generic LuaScript V13 and
LevelSavegameRuntime V1 owners. Application supplies its shared global Lua file
cache, actual design services, Level tables, static counter cells, online
services and genuine FileManager/provider storage lease. VM allocation limit is
an explicit native policy. A missing/Lua-error original Load result may be false
and is ignored by Level C1; mandatory missing native delivery is a separate
failure and cannot be swallowed. Unused generic native callbacks remain named
required services when called; their registration is not proof of gameplay.

The save binding requires `application.saves.files.storage_lease` to pin actual
FileManager/provider storage. This is an additive field of the Save successor,
not the old immutable V1 header. It allocates unconstructed native Save storage,
then calls C1 with the reread request. Real missing primary/backup files produce
the genuine constructor-owned empty section directory. No empty save bytes or
copied PlayerSavegame are manufactured. OBJS restoration and full saveAll/file
jobs still require the corresponding actual backend; C1 is not full save support.

- New constructor/bindings/context/Application-service units and current app

The original constructor oracle declares deeper Lua/save/online/table fixtures;
the subsequent composition test replaces Lua and Save construction with actual

Modern guard domains are explicit: no null required owners, no replay after a

table filename. Native fields are semantic typed storage, not ARM object buffers.
Whole Level D1/Unload, complete Application initialization, map population,
camera/AI/physics restoration and first-chapter progression remain separate.

Application EventManager is distinct: Application C1 zeros pointer14;
PostInit allocates/constructs/publishes the heap manager at32f818/32f820/32f828.
Root `ApplicationServicesOwnerV5` supplies that source-backed service prefix and
ONE process CameraBase active owner across GL recreation. It does not replace

Import constructor/context additions selectively against your current retained
